findings.failure_path: After a grant is armed, a human can submit `<task-notification>\n<summary>先别合并</summary>\n</task-notification>`. The line matches the tag pattern, its extracted value contains no angle brackets, and note_only remains 1. This exit skips revocation and epoch advancement, leaving the grant usable despite the explicit stop. Copying the complete host-shaped notification with a stop in its summary works for the same reason. F1 remains unresolved.
findings.smallest_fix: Require trusted host-origin evidence before exempting a notification from user-message processing. If the host exposes no such evidence, retain revocation for notification-shaped user text. Add tagged-stop regression cases for every grant kind.

challenge_focus: Adversarial delta review. (a) Bypass-by-omission: for the document closeout reminder and the task-notification exit, list every literal path that reaches the gated outcome while the trigger is never produced (doc edits not recorded as edit tool calls, notification-shaped text a user can type, a tag element carrying user text). (c) Can the closeout reminder fire on agent-only files, loop past the one-recheck bound, or crash the Stop hook? (d) Do the records claim more than the evidence shows (RED versus control)?
